column2: A Village in Need

The harvest failed here before the first frost. The village headman offers me the last of his salt fish and a place by the fire, then asks, quietly, whether the Avatar can mend a roof before he can mend a field. The spoiled grain is already turning black in the storehouse.
Spend the day helping them rebuild
Offer a quiet blessing and counsel
A Whisper Beyond the Veil

At dusk the wind drops. A pale light moves between the pines, too low for a lantern and too steady for a firefly. The villagers have left a bowl of rice at the tree line. Something out there is waiting to see whether I will answer.
Listen carefully to the spirit
Leave with a respectful bow
A Test of Discipline

The old bending master has cleared the square and set a row of clay pots along the wall. He asks me to fill them without cracking a single one. A crowd has gathered for a show of power. He has given me a lesson in restraint instead.
Focus on precision and practice
Meet the challenge head-on
Travellers on the Road

A family of four stands at the ford with a handcart and a lame ox. They say the road ahead is held by men who take everything and leave the carts. The father has a purse, but he keeps looking at his children when he offers it.
Escort them to safety
Accept a small travel purse
A Dispute at the Crossing

Two villages have met at the old stone bridge, and both have brought axes. The miller says the upstream village raised the toll without warning. The upstream headman says the miller's carts broke the parapet and never paid to mend it. The bridge is narrow enough that no one can pass without the other's leave.
Hear both sides and judge fairly
Find a compromise they can accept
My Animal Companion

My companion stops at the edge of a burned field and will not go on. Its ears are flat, and its nose points at a stand of dead oak where the road bends. The path it wants is narrow and half hidden by briars. The road ahead is shorter.
Follow its lead patiently
Trust it and press on bravely
A Moment of Stillness

For once the courtyard is empty. No petition, no master, no runner from the capital. I sit on the cold stones and listen to the fountain until the water sounds like a voice. By dusk I have no answers, only a quieter mind.
Remain in meditation a little longer
Return to the world refreshed
Trouble on the Trail
Three men have a merchant backed against a cart on the coast road. They see me and two of them run. The third spits, draws a knife, and asks whether the Avatar bleeds like other men.
Stand firm and protect the merchant
Get everyone clear without bloodshed
An Unexpected Lesson

An old woman on the road watches me bend a fallen tree out of the way. She says nothing until I finish, then points to the nest I crushed in the branches. 'The wind is easy,' she says. 'Knowing where not to blow is the work.'
Ask to practice the lesson together
Thank her and reflect on her words
A Festival in My Honour

The town has hung paper lanterns across the square and set a place for me at the head table. The children want me to bend a flame for them. The elders want to tell me what the last Avatar did wrong. The musicians have already started, and no one has asked me to leave.
Join the celebration and meet the people
Donate to the festivities and slip away early
The Debt of a Friend

A chief I pulled from a frozen river ten years ago has come to collect. He means to march on a neighbor whose walls are higher and whose men are more. He does not ask me to fight. He asks me to stand beside him where his people can see, so that the old debt will look like a promise.
Stand with him, and try to end it quickly
Refuse, and tell him plainly why
The Broken Student

A boy I trained in the old courtyard now leads a band of cutthroats on the eastern road. The villagers he robs have started leaving my name on the empty grain sacks, as if I might hear it. He was quick to learn. He was quicker to take a blow badly.
Go after him and bring him home
Leave him to the law
An Old Enemy's Grave

The grave is a low mound behind a shepherd's wall, marked by a stone with no name left on it. I know the place. I put him here. The grass has grown over the spot where his sword fell, and a dog is sleeping against the stone.
Speak the words of parting
Leave a token and walk on
The Town That Fears Me

The town has barred its gates and hung a bundle of dried herbs over every door. They say the drought came with me. A crowd is gathering in the square with hoes and wood axes. The headman is trying to keep them behind the well.
Walk into the square unarmed
Leave them to their fear
The Scholar's Doubt

A scholar has filled three tables with scrolls about the past Avatars. He says, politely, that the last three men who claimed to be the Avatar were hanged. Then he asks me to name the wife of an Avatar who died four hundred years ago. I have no proof but my own word.
Answer him honestly
Turn his questions back on him
The Fading Spirit

The river has shrunk to a brown trickle, and the fish lie on their sides in the shallows. A spirit waits in the reeds, thin as a heron's shadow. It does not speak. It only opens its hands, and I feel how little it has left.
Give the spirit part of my strength
Let the river find its own course
The Runaway

A child has followed me for two days, sleeping in the stable and eating what the cooks leave out. The guardian's account says the child is stubborn and prone to lies. The child's account says the guardian's belt is not for show. Both accounts include the same bruised wrist.
Take them home and speak to the guardian
Find the child a kinder home
A Wedding at the Edge of the World

A friend from the road is to be married in a village so far north that the invitation arrived with the first snow. They ask for no gift. They want me to stand at the back of the hall and bless the union, and they have already saved me a place at the family table.
Attend and bless the union
Send a gift and a letter
The Titan's Challenge

A fighter from beyond the western islands has set up a ring outside the town and broken three local champions in a morning. He says he has come to fight the Avatar. He says it loudly, and the crowd is already collecting coins.
Accept, and end it quickly
Refuse, and offer to train him instead
Smoke on the Horizon

Smoke is rising from the eastern ridge, and the wind is pushing it toward a town with no wall and one dry well. The first roofs are an hour away, perhaps less. The town's bells have started, and the road out is already crowded with carts.
Bend the wind and the flames myself
Lead the evacuation from the front
